title: Need help with figuring how to make a good 3-d terrain map with AI(Fable)
author: Puzzled-War-1615
selftext:
Has anyone had any luck creating a good 3-d map/heightmap with AI? I'm trying to create one with for a survival game I'm creating and have just struggled to get Fable to understand exactly what I want. I've created a terrain map in Aseprite(as shown, although this is an old version no nobody takes my map :D) along with a zone map and a markdown document that describes what each zone is, what it looks like, etc. Then fable has attempted to create a good heightmap for me to use in UE5. It really struggled to do hills/mountains/islands or any kind of sharper terrain features. As it is now, I'm going to have to spend a couple weeks just sitting in landscape mode in UE5 trying my best to figure out how to fix it's mistakes 

I feel like either it's just not good to translating this to a good heightmap, i'm not being descriptive enough in my markdown document, or I'm taking an entirely wrong approach with how to use AI in map creation.

Anyone have any suggestions on the process they have used successfully with AI?

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
I can't even tell what projection this is. No indication of what is a mountain, what is a valley or a field etc. Is it perspective? is it top down? I have no idea.

How do you expect AI to turn this into a height map if someone can't even look at it and understand what camera or projection it is? I .e. why a sphere? is it a globe? 

Nobody is going to steal your map.

replies.author: Puzzled-War-1615
replies.body: Ah my apologies, I described it all to the bot, along with the hex color. Brown is mountain, orange is hill. Etc, I think I had 20 or so terrain types.

replies.author: HaMMeReD
replies.body:
If you want AI to "work nicely" it needs to understand your content. An image with a legend doesn't make much sense.

Maybe describe a bunch of concept art/hero images for your world in a thread, get vantage points, landmarks and build a world like that by "moving" around it with image-gen.

Then when you are happy with the concept and vantage points and such you've created. The take your 4-5 best images and give it back to the agent or chat and ask for a heightmap of that world, based on the photos/reference frames.

comments.author: LeafyWolf
comments.body: After a few iterations, I've settled on plate tectonics + epoch simulations.  That gives decent elevation variation...and then you need hydrology for the rest.

Check out mapng.com. You can make height maps of places on Earth. You can even get the satellite view as textures. 

Then ask Claude to read the height map and apply the texture.
